specific_checks.a_x402_non_evm: Yes. The spec has SVM exact/upto/batch-settlement schemes with Ed25519 vouchers, plus 14 more non-EVM exact schemes. SIWX supports solana with ed25519.
specific_checks.b_wba_algorithms: draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-01 sets no mandatory-to-implement algorithm. Any IANA-registered RFC 9421 algorithm is allowed (§5.2), and HMAC MUST NOT be used (§6.4). Ed25519 appears only in examples and test vectors, alongside rsa-pss-sha512.
specific_checks.c_mpp_methods: See MPP.algorithms. Core uses only server-side HMAC-SHA256. Methods use EIP-712/secp256k1, Tempo secp256k1/P256/WebAuthn, Ed25519 (Solana, NEAR), Lightning preimages, Stripe SPT bearer tokens, and card RSA-OAEP-256 encryption.
specific_checks.d_x401: Verifier-signed OpenID4VP request (JAR) over the W3C Digital Credentials API with a DCQL query, sent in PROOF-REQUEST/PROOF-RESPONSE/PROOF-RESULT headers. Agent binding and the OAuth token exchange are optional. x401 sets no algorithms.
specific_checks.e_vi: ES256 MUST at all layers; _sd_alg sha-256; EdDSA deferred to a future version.
specific_checks.f_a2a_card: JWS with JCS. alg MUST be present but is unrestricted (examples ES256, RS256). kid MUST be present; jku is optional.
specific_checks.g_mcp_agent_key: No agent signing key in core. The only client key is the optional private_key_jwt (MAY), with JWKS from the CIMD. Extensions add JWT client assertions and IdP-signed ID-JAGs.

note_vs_spec_disagreements.spec: The TAP spec page sets no algorithm list. Message signature examples use Ed25519, the consumer object example uses PS256, and the ID token says PS256 is preferred to RS256. The sample code uses rsa-pss-sha256 (RFC 9421 name), not PS256. 'Ed25519 or RSA-PSS' describes the sample code, not a spec constraint.

note_vs_spec_disagreements.note: stacks-new-combinations.md L65 ('Delegation hops carry a DataIntegrityProof with eddsa-jcs-2022 (10.5 item 3)') and README.md L256 ('KYA-OS Ed25519')
note_vs_spec_disagreements.spec: Correct for the Entity Card §10.5 profile. Core SPEC.md §6.2 uses a bespoke JCS+Ed25519 proof labelled Ed25519Signature2020, which the spec says a W3C Data Integrity verifier will not verify. Entity Card proofs also allow ES256 (§8.4), so 'KYA-OS = Ed25519 only' is true of core only.

note_vs_spec_disagreements.note: chain-stacks.md L157 / stacks-new-combinations.md L157: 'the WBA convention is Ed25519'
note_vs_spec_disagreements.spec: WBA draft-01 has no Ed25519 requirement. Ed25519 is a deployment convention (UCP signatures.md L99 says the same, non-normatively).
Only the Session JWT must be ES256. Client assertions and delegations may be ES256 or PS384 (§4.1, §5.2), and the operator signature follows WBA (any algorithm).

note_vs_spec_disagreements.note: Notes treat ACP request Signature as an asymmetric signature with out-of-band algorithm
note_vs_spec_disagreements.spec: This matches the RFCs, but the 2026-04-17 and unreleased OpenAPI describe the request Signature header as 'HMAC signature for webhook verification', and delegate_payment says both MUST (§2.2) and RECOMMENDED (header list). The spec is internally inconsistent; the notes do not flag it.

note_vs_spec_disagreements.spec: Matches specification.md L154-157, but security_and_privacy_considerations.md L145-148 allows a deterministic algorithm if the checkout carries a salt. UCP ap2-mandates.md L144-156 flags this as an internal inconsistency.
